name: FL-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Polymarket prices Democratic chances at just 4%
Republican candidate outraised Democrat by roughly 35-to-1
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
model.rationale: This is a heavily Republican open seat where the GOP nominee has a massive fundraising edge and prediction markets give the Democrat only a 4% chance. With no polls or expert ratings to move the picture, the partisan lean and money advantage point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving the Republican nominee could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving this southwest Florida seat to run for governor, creating an open race in a district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. Jim Schwartzel, the Republican nominee, has raised over two million dollars and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Victor Arias, who has raised under sixty thousand. An independent candidate trails far behind in both money and visibility.

Prediction markets give the Republican nominee roughly a 94% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, the fundraising gap, and market pricing, all of which point to a Republican hold with a margin in the mid-teens.
